finding.summary: New shared-reader call site bypasses the repo's existing safe CRDT-record reader (`safeWorksheetRecordEntries`), leaving the hardening it advertises half-applied
finding.evidence: The delta rewrites the cross-sheet resolver to use `buildMergeCoverMap`, with a comment claiming it "survives a key that is not a cell reference and a span that is not two positive integers" so the resolver does not hang the tab on a hostile map. But it feeds it `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {})` — the raw CRDT record — while every other reader of this exact field goes through the shared helper `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:977, 1072, 1277, 1291, 1309; packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:193 in this same diff). That helper exists precisely because `Object.entries` on a Yorkie record can throw a duplicate-own-keys error (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:47-61), which here throws *outside* the new defensive walk and takes the resolver (and the tab's cross-sheet formulas) down for the hostile-map case the change is meant to survive. verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted (sheet-view.tsx:1242-1243 feeds raw `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {})` into `buildMergeCoverMap`, and `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` exists at worksheet-record.ts:47-61), but it is not a blocking design-fit defect. (a) The hardening the change advertises is fully applied here: `buildMergeCoverMap` (merging.ts:167-204) drops non-integer/non-positive spans (isCountableMergeSpan, :130-139/:179), budget-unaffordable spans (:180), non-parseable keys (:183-190) and non-round-tripping keys (:194). (b) The canonical design doc prescribes exactly this shape — docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:188-193 and merging.ts:156-159 say the frontend resolver "walks the same raw CRDT map" through the shared builder — so there is no divergence from the documented design, no reinvented module, and no unmet acceptance criterion. (c) The remaining gap (duplicate-own-keys TypeError from Yorkie proxy enumeration) is a separate hazard from the hostile-map hazards this change targets, is pre-existing and pervasive in this file — sheet-view.tsx:246, :247, :273, :1160 and especially :1278-1281, where the adjacent cross-sheet formula resolver walks `ws.cells` with bare `Object.entries` in the same wiring block, so fixing only line 1243 would not keep the tab alive on such a document. Under this lens's rubric that makes it "reuse that was available but not required" (explicitly minor, non-blocking); the missing try/catch itself is a line-level defensive-coding point deferred to the correctness lens.

finding.summary: Published API reference still documents the old freeze bound and merge rules this change narrows. `packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:650-651` states `rows` is `integer 0..1000000` and `cols` `0..18278`, but `parseFreeze` now rejects anything above `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1,000) with a 400; line 653 says `GET`/`PUT` return `{rows, cols}` without noting that `PUT freeze` may now answer with a *snapped* boundary different from the one requested; the merges rule table at 688-694 lists only the per-span 100,000 cap and gains neither the new `MaxMergeEntries` (10,000) nor `MaxMergeCoveredCells` (1e6) 400s nor the new 409 for a map that straddles the tab's freeze. An external client following the shipped docs now gets 400/409 on requests the docs call legal, and a previously-valid `{"rows": 5000}` call breaks silently at the doc level.

verdict.reason: The REST API reference already documents every item the finding calls missing. rest-api.md:651-652 type `rows`/`cols` as `integer 0..1000` (the finding's quoted `0..1000000` / `0..18278` text is not in the file), and :656 states the 1,000-per-axis ceiling with `400` above it, matching parseFreeze's `max: MaxSnappedFreeze` at worksheet-settings.ts:69-75. rest-api.md:658 explicitly warns in bold that `PUT` may store a snapped boundary different from the requested one (including the release-to-0 case), and :660 covers legacy deeper-than-1,000 `GET` values. The merges rule table carries `Map size` = 10,000 entries -> 400 (:701) and `Map area` = 1,000,000 covered cells -> 400 (:702), i.e. MaxMergeEntries and MaxMergeCoveredCells as enforced via mergeBudgetError (worksheet-settings.ts:138-144, 189-192), plus the new freeze-straddle `409` at :703 (and the move-path variant at :632). The doc is in sync with the narrowed validation, so there is no spec/doc mismatch to block on.
